Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
122 AM EST Sat Nov 21 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Temperatures have trended cooler for today and forecasted rain 
amounts have increased for parts of NE Georgia and the SC Upstate.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. Rain chances increase today and tonight with beneficial rainfall
possible across much of our forecast area.
2. Much cooler from Tuesday onward with increasing precipitation
chances during mid-week, and the possibility of frozen precipitation
over the NC mountains.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: Rain chances increase today and tonight with beneficial 
rainfall possible across much of our forecast area. 

Broad upper ridging remains over our region but will steadily shift 
east over the weekend. Broad sfc high pressure currently centered to 
our north will also shift E/NE as a disorganized area of low pressure
begins to organize and drift northward and over our area today and
Sunday. The latest model guidance still has the primary sfc low de-
velopment occurring just off the Southeast Coast. However, some amount
of secondary development/enhanced isentropic lift over the stable sfc 
wedge is likely to occur inland along the baroclinic zone over our area.
PoPs have increased to likely for the bulk of our CWA for Sat night and 
early Sunday with rainfall amounts in the 0.1 to 0.5 inch range. Amounts 
have trended up the most over our NE Georgia and western Upstate zones.  

Otherwise, high temperatures are expected to remain near-normal across 
our area today under thickening cloud cover. Highs warm above normal
again on Sunday with rain chances diminishing as the day progresses. 
Monday is still fcst to be the warmest day of the next 7 days, with 
highs 10+ degrees above climatology as skies clear and downslope/com-
pressional warming develops in advance of an approaching frontal bndy. 
This front could bring some brief, light showers to the NC mtns Monday
afternoon/evening, but will otherwise be moisture-limited.


Key message 2: Much cooler from Tuesday onward with increasing
precipitation chances during mid-week, and the possibility
of frozen precipitation over the NC mountains. 

Height falls and an attendant, mostly dry cold front cross the
region Monday night into Tuesday, bringing much cooler temperatures.
Temperatures are expected to be near-to-below normal from Tuesday 
thru the end of the week. Otherwise, the long-range models suggest 
a low-confidence fcst from roughly mid-week onward, as a highly
amplified and complex upper air pattern evolves over the CONUS, 
with little agreement between the deterministic models. There  
appears to be some consensus amongst the models that a Miller-B 
type low will develop somewhere off the Southeast Coast Wednesday 
into Thursday, with precip chances trending higher across our fcst
area during this period. Precip amounts remain more uncertain, but
it's looking more likely that a good portion of our CWA could get
rainfall. Also, if enough cold air is in place over the NC mtns 
early Wednesday, they could see some wintry precip at the onset.
Any accumulations of frozen precip would likely be minimal.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: OVC VFR cirrus is noted over the terminals as 
of 06Z. Should see VFR and dry conditions linger through at least 
the morning hours before cigs gradually lower as rain spreads over 
the terminals from south to north this afternoon into this evening. 
Maintained PROB30s for the onset of -RA as confidence on timing 
remains low. Once -RA develops then it should stick around through 
the end of the TAF period so went with prevailing -RA when PROB30s 
end. Vsbys should remain mostly VFR, dropping only to 5SM or 6SM but 
could end up lower where heavier pockets of RA develop. Cigs should 
lower to low-end VFR later this morning before dropping to MVFR 
levels this afternoon into this evening. Could see pockets of IFR 
cigs develop late tonight, especially at KAND and KCLT. Winds will 
remain NE east of the mountains while gradually increasing in speed 
through late this afternoon/early evening, with 20-25 kt gusts 
developing around or just after daybreak. Winds at KAVL should 
remain calm through the morning hours before picking up out of the E 
this afternoon. Winds at KAVL should toggle more NW this evening. 
Wind speeds should be lighter at KAVL compared to the other 
terminals east of the mountains, with no gusts expected. 

Outlook: Rain chances and associated restrictions should linger 
through Sunday. A cold front may bring rain chances back along the 
NC/TN border Monday before better rain chances, and possible 
restrictions, return area-wide by mid-week.
